title: EXP-012 — Persistent Form Variable Definition Retention With Approved Session Establishment
objective: Using one new User-scope classic BuildFromScratch Form, establish or confirm a usable Mongoose session before any artifact mutation, then create exactly one Form variable with Global=False and Persistent=True, record its exact visible design-time definition, perform exactly one ordinary Designer Save, verify the definition remains immediately after Save, close only the target Form tab, reopen the exact same User-scoped Form through a previously verified supported Designer reopen path, and verify the same design-time variable definition is still present. The result is limited strictly to design-time definition retention; it must not test or claim runtime value persistence, temporary-variable behavior, cache behavior, or physical storage provenance.

in_scope: At the very beginning of the experiment, before any Mongoose artifact mutation, either confirm an already-live Mongoose session or establish one through the previously documented supported Mongoose/Web Client sign-in flow; do not expose credential values.
After session readiness is established, prove the session is live with an observable server-backed check and prove editing scope is User.
Prove FX_FormVariableLab02 is absent exact and case-insensitive before mutation through the live Select Form/inventory surface.
Create exactly one new User-scope classic BuildFromScratch Form named FX_FormVariableLab02 using the verified basic-form recipe with Save Template unchecked.
Open Details > Variables on FX_FormVariableLab02 and create exactly one Form variable named FX_PersistentRetentionVar.
Set Global=False, Persistent=True, and design-time Value=Seed-Persist-B, recording every visible variable-definition field before Save.
Perform exactly one ordinary Designer Save after variable creation and prove the Designer returns to a clean state.
Immediately re-read Details > Variables and compare all visible definition fields with the pre-Save baseline.
Close only FX_FormVariableLab02 using its ordinary Designer Form-tab close control and verify there is no unsaved-change prompt.
Reopen FX_FormVariableLab02 using a previously verified supported Designer reopen path such as Form-menu recent forms or Select Form, not a direct cold URL.
Prove the reopened version is the same User-scoped target using Name + ScopeType + ScopeName.
Reopen Details > Variables and compare the variable definition against the pre-Save baseline.
Capture screenshots and read-only diagnostics under evidence/EXP-012/ and update only the EXP-012 experiment record plus its evidence directory.
out_of_scope: Replaying, repairing, changing, or promoting EXP-004 or EXP-011.
Treating EXP-012 as a replay of EXP-011; EXP-011 never reached the semantic operation.
Testing Persistent=False behavior or creating a comparison variable.
Executing Form logic to read, mutate, initialize, or otherwise test the runtime value of the variable.
Testing whether a persistent variable value survives executions, Form close/reopen, logout/login, application-session replacement, or any runtime lifecycle.
Regenerate Form or any second save mechanism.
Unload All Global Form Objects, deliberate IDO metadata unloading, cache-clearing experiments, or User Preferences.
Caption, Description, component, collection, binding, validator, event handler, script, data-source, IDO-definition, localized-String, or FormSync experiments.
Site, Group, or Vendor Default editing scope.
Modification of any existing FX_ artifact.
Creation or modification of reusable recipes, AGENTS.md, environment files, or other experiment records.
Physical Forms-database provenance, direct database inspection or mutation, undocumented APIs, or internal session manipulation.
Any claim that successful design-time recovery proves durable database storage, cache eviction, or runtime value persistence.

prohibited_actions: Creating, modifying or deleting any non-FX_ artifact
Starting any other experiment or replay
Modifying production data or disabling security
Do not create, modify, or delete any non-FX_ Mongoose artifact.
Do not modify any existing FX_ artifact.
Do not start another experiment or replay.
Do not modify production data or weaken security.
Do not read, print, log, screenshot, or otherwise expose credential values.

Session establishment is allowed only before the first Mongoose artifact mutation. Once FX_FormVariableLab02 creation begins, do not login, Sign In/OK, deliberately reauthenticate, logout, restart the browser, or deliberately replace the session; if the session expires after mutation begins, stop and record the blocker.
Do not use Regenerate Form and do not perform more than one ordinary Designer Save after variable creation.
Do not execute logic intended to read, modify, or prove runtime variable-value persistence.
Do not create a Persistent=False comparison variable.
Do not invoke Form > Definition > Unload All Global Form Objects or any deliberate cache/metadata-clear command.
Do not open, change, or save User Preferences.
Do not create components, handlers, scripts, validators, bindings, data sources, collections, IDOs, localized Strings, or FormSync artifacts.
Do not use direct cold ?MGForm= navigation to reopen the target.
Do not make any replay_verified classification; this is an original experiment.

acceptance_checks.description: Before any Mongoose artifact mutation, evidence proves either the inherited session was already live or the supported session-establishment flow was completed; afterward a live server-backed check succeeds, the Web Client is usable, editing scope is User, and FX_FormVariableLab02 is absent exact and case-insensitive in the live inventory.

Exactly one new User-scope classic BuildFromScratch Form named FX_FormVariableLab02 exists after creation through the verified basic-form recipe with Save Template unchecked; creation and inventory evidence prove exactly one target.

Before Save, Details > Variables visibly contains exactly one experiment-created variable named FX_PersistentRetentionVar with Global=False, Persistent=True, and Value=Seed-Persist-B where Value is exposed; all visible definition fields are recorded as the comparison baseline.
Exactly one ordinary Designer Save is performed after variable creation, no Regenerate Form or second Save occurs, and evidence proves the Designer returns to a clean state.
Immediately after the ordinary Save, Details > Variables still contains FX_PersistentRetentionVar and every visible recorded design-time definition field equals the AC-3 baseline.
FX_FormVariableLab02 is closed only through its ordinary Designer Form-tab close control, with no unsaved-change prompt and no explicit unload/cache/metadata-clear action.

FX_FormVariableLab02 is deliberately reopened through a previously verified supported Designer reopen path rather than direct cold URL navigation, and the loaded version is proven by Name + ScopeType + ScopeName to be the same User-scoped target.
After reopen, Details > Variables contains exactly the expected FX_PersistentRetentionVar definition and every recorded design-time definition field equals the AC-3 baseline.

The experiment record explicitly classifies the result only as observed design-time definition retention or non-retention for the tested Global=False/Persistent=True variable and makes no runtime-value-persistence, temporary-variable, cache, database-durability, or storage-provenance claim.

Final repository/worktree audit proves experiment-attributable changes are confined to the EXP-012 record and evidence/EXP-012/, with no recipe, AGENTS.md, environment, other experiment, existing FX_ artifact, or non-FX_ artifact modified.

Evidence and the experiment record prove that any session-establishment action occurred only before the first Mongoose artifact mutation; after FX_FormVariableLab02 creation began, no login, Sign In/OK, deliberate reauthentication, logout, browser restart, or deliberate session replacement occurred.

notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261003-023021-swqQ. Rationale: EXP-011 never reached the variable experiment: it stopped at preflight because the inherited Mongoose session was already expired and its reviewed boundaries prohibited restoring that session after run start. The smallest useful next step is a new experiment using a different, explicitly documented precondition: session establishment is permitted only at the beginning of the experiment, before any Mongoose artifact mutation, and the semantic experiment begins only after a live session, User editing scope, and target absence are proven. This preserves the intended variable-definition question without treating the blocked EXP-011 as a replay and without relaxing controls after mutation begins. It also directly follows the unresolved variable-definition work from EXP-004 while using the verified basic-form creation procedure.
